articles.title: Brooklyn building collapse leaves at least 2 people dead and 17 injured
articles.summary: At least two people were killed and 17 others injured Wednesday, when a three-story building collapsed in the Flatbush neighborhood of Brooklyn in New York City. The four-unit apartment building crumpled into a construction site next to it at about 4 p.m. ET in the Flatbush area. Seven of the casualties were children, Reuters reported, with at least 10 people taken to a hospital. Authorities did not confirm if any of the children were among those killed. Rescuers searched for survivors into the night with about 250 first responders at the scene. “We’ll continue to look until we find everybody,” FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said. One resident, Anderson Velez, told the New York Post he was at work in the Bronx when his wife called him and said their children, ages 7 and 2, were trapped. “She called me when the building collapsed while she was inside with rubble on top of her. She was screaming for someone to help get my son out and then the call cut off,” he said, confirming his family was now safe. Crews worked throughout the night to rescue those still trapped inside the collapsed building. New York television station WABC-TV reported that a pregnant woman was pulled from the rubble hours after the collapse. The 1930s building fell into an adjoining construction site, where excavation work was ongoing. The cause of the collapse is under investigation, said John Esposito, the city's fire department chief. He said rescue teams may need to take several days to search the site for all potential victims. The interiors of apartments in an adjacent damaged building were exposed after the building collapsed. Anadolu via Getty Images Where the bridge collapse in Brooklyn. Anadolu via Getty Images Officials have described the search and rescue mission as “very dangerous,” with firefighters and police officers punching holes through rubble in the search for survivors. "Multiple people from the building and the construction site were trapped," Bonsignore said. "This will be a prolonged operation. Collapse operations are extremely dangerous. Every move is choreographed and critically important to patient outcomes and member safety. Members have been working methodically and haven't stopped since they arrived." No official cause for the collapse has been released. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said at a news conference that rescue workers arrived on the scene within one minute of receiving the 911 call. He also confirmed the fatalities and said that injured people had been transported to local hospitals. "This has been an incredibly challenging and fast-moving situation - with precarious wreckage to navigate and dangerous voids beneath the surface," he said, adding, “This type of rescue is exactly what the FDNY trains for.” First responders search through rubble and debris at the scene of a building collapse in Brooklyn. Anadolu via Getty Images He also asked New Yorkers to “please take a moment to pray for those who passed away today and all of those who are mourning their loss." The husband of a pregnant woman told reporters she had been pulled alive from the rubble. “She is alive, she is still alive. I am very happy,” he can be heard saying in video footage shared by WABC-TV. Earlier, the man had been seen frantically looking for her, "I've heard nothing. She's inside the building. She's pregnant,” he said. An eyewitness, Melissa Orna, told The New York Times : "The whole building started shaking, and then it just fell." articles.title: 'I kept the faith:' Democrat Scott Colom flips Mississippi Senate seat in historic upset
articles.summary: Mississippi Democrat Scott Colom narrowly defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith on Wednesday to flip another Senate seat for Democrats and become the first Black candidate elected to the U.S. Senate from Mississippi in more than 140 years. According to figures from the Associated Press, Colom — who will also be Mississippi's first Democratic senator since 1989 — won 49.2% of the vote. Hyde-Smith finished with 48.7%. "There were times that I couldn't get donors to answer the phone," Colom told supporters as they celebrated his historic upset late Wednesday night . "They did not believe a moment like this was possible, but I kept the faith." Mississippi — one of the reddest states in the country — wasn't really on the national radar prior to Nov. 3. President Trump won the state by 23 percentage points in 2024 — his third straight win there. Looking ahead to the 2026 Senate race, analysts said it was a "likely Republican" hold . Barely anyone bothered to poll it . But by the end of Election Night, Colom and Hyde-Smith were separated by just 65 votes, shocking the nation. Colom's win expands Democrats' total number of Senate seats to 55 and cements the party's best overall midterm performance since 1974 — a rout that has seen the GOP lose control of the Senate, the House and statehouses across the country . As lawyers, operatives and legal observers descended on Mississippi to watch officials count every last ballot, Colom repeatedly expressed confidence that his campaign would prevail, flooding the airwaves and attending at least eight post-election events. "It's very clear the direction of this," he told reporters on Friday . Colom picked up that thread in Wednesday's victory speech. "I've been telling everybody that we're going to win this election," he said. "I was saying it 8 or 9 months ago. But every time I said it, I pointed out that people were going to give me too much credit for it because it's not something that I did. It's something that we did.  All I did was have the courage to imagine a night like this. I had the courage to believe in Mississippi." Hyde-Smith conceded to Colom in a video posted on X Wednesday evening : "While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said. "I want to congratulate Scott Colom and wish him well as he takes on the tremendous responsibility of representing our great state." Alaska is now the only undecided Senate race. Democrat Mary Peltola leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan 48.9% to 47.3% with 84% of the vote counted, according to the latest AP figures. Who is Scott Colom? Colom, 43, was born in Columbus, Miss., to two lawyers who also participated in politics. In 1987, his father, Wilbur, ran for state treasurer as a Republican; his mother, Dorothy, served as the first Black Chancery Court judge in their home district. Colom earned his JD from the University of Wisconsin in 2009 and went on to serve as the first Black justice court judge in Lowndes County, Miss., before becoming the first Black city prosecutor in Columbus. In 2015, Colom defeated a nearly 30-year incumbent to become the first Black district attorney elected in a majority-white voting district in Mississippi history. He has since prosecuted a number of high-profile murder and sexual assault cases. Colom gives an update about his Senate race on Nov. 4, 2026 in Jackson, Miss. Rogelio V. Solis/Getty Images In 2022, President Joe Biden nominated Colom to serve as federal judge for the Northern District of Mississippi. Leading Magnolia State Republicans — including Sen. Roger Wicker and former Govs. Phil Bryant and Haley Barbour — backed Colom's nomination. "I have known two generations of the Colom family for over 20 years and believe Scott Colom possesses the discernment to be a fair and exemplary judge," Bryant told the New York Times . But Hyde-Smith blocked Colom's nomination in the Senate, citing support his 2015 campaign received from a political action committee funded by George Soros and claiming that he favored allowing transgender athletes to compete in girls' and women's sports. The White House characterized Hyde-Smith's concerns as " spurious ." In a letter to Hyde-Smith urging her to reconsider, Colom confirmed that he had signed a letter with other prosecutors condemning efforts to criminalize gender-affirming care for transgender people, but insisted that their joint statement "did not comment on legislation specifically related to participation in athletics." Colom also said he had not known about Soros's contributions to the Mississippi Safety and Justice PAC "until I read about them in my hometown paper." Colom's unsuccessful nomination was returned to Biden on Jan. 3, 2024. In September 2025, Colom announced his U.S. Senate candidacy. How Colom won Hyde-Smith, 67, is a former lobbyist and state legislator who was serving as Mississippi's agriculture and commerce commissioner when she was appointed to the U.S. Senate in 2018 following the resignation of Republican Sen. Thad Cochran. She won a 2018 special election and a 2020 full-term election, and she has served in the Senate ever since. There were signs before Election Day that Hyde-Smith might be vulnerable to "voter apathy," as one Mississippi State University political science professor recently put it . Sen. Wicker won reelection in 2024 by 25 points; Hyde-Smith's margin of victory in 2020 was less than half that. And while the only polls made public this cycle showed Hyde-Smith ahead , her leads were stuck in the single digits — no survey put her support above 50%. One April Democratic poll showed Hyde-Smith trailing a hypothetical "someone else" 33% to 53%. Hyde-Smith speaks at a campaign event in Corinth, Miss., on Oct. 26, 2026. Madison Thorn/Bloomberg via Getty Images Regardless, Hyde-Smith seemed content to coast to reelection, barely bothering to appear on the campaign trail. But Colom didn't have that luxury — and when he cut a viral campaign ad about beef prices in mid-October, the tide started to turn. Asked earlier this year about soaring costs, including the price of beef, Hyde-Smith told local TV station WLOX that "all commodities go through peaks and valleys," but "you have so many proteins to choose from." In the final weeks of the campaign, Colom seized on Hyde-Smith's remark about "proteins" to mock her with a spot featuring incredulous Mississippians grilling burgers, dining out and shopping for groceries — and saying they'd rather "pick another senator instead" (along with other, more colorful language). The video has since racked up nearly 19 million views on Colom's X account . She done lost her damn mind. pic.twitter.com/wHPt4PSAob — Scott Colom (@scott_colom) October 13, 2026 When the ad took off, national Democrats sprang into action. The Senate Majority PAC poured $2.2 million into the race; Senate Democrats' campaign arm contributed another $500,000. Former President Barack Obama filmed an endorsement ad. Former President Bill Clinton, former Vice President Kamala Harris and Sens. Cory Booker of New Jersey and Raphael Warnock of Georgia rushed to Mississippi to rally with Colom. In response, Republicans were forced to play defense, sending Trump to Mississippi in the final days of the campaign (along with cash infusions of their own). In the end, it wasn't enough to get Hyde-Smith over the line. When Trump came to Mississippi, Colom attended his event to talk to rally-goers about health care, grocery bills and gas prices. "I got the best message ever for Republican voters in Mississippi," he told CNN afterward. "I'm going to get you what you were promised in 2024. You were promised lower grocery prices on Day One. That's what I will fight for. You were promised no more endless wars. That's what I will fight for. You were promised the full and transparent release of the Epstein files. That's what I will fight for." articles.title: Famed ship heads for afterlife as artificial reef in deliberate sinking off Florida
articles.summary: By Steve Gorman Nov 11 (Reuters) - Famed ocean liner SS United States, the largest passenger ship ever built in America and the world's fastest, headed for the sea floor near Florida on Wednesday in a deliberate sinking designed to transform the vessel into the world's biggest artificial reef. The finale to a ‌yearlong process preparing the ship to meet its destiny, 75 years after it was first launched at sea, was presented in a livestream with aerial views of ‌the once-grand vessel's rusted hulk, stripped of its two smokestacks, quietly, slowly settling into calm waters of the Gulf of Mexico before succumbing to the deep. The ship, measuring nearly 1,000 feet (300 m) from stem to stern, was ​surrounded by onlookers and safety crews aboard dozens of tugboats and recreational vessels that accompanied the ocean liner as it was towed out to sea for its final voyage. By then, work crews had spent months removing all environmentally unsafe materials from the ship, including residual fuel, wiring, glass, ductwork and other non-metal items, as well as any objects that could pose entanglement hazards for scuba divers. The crews then cut holes strategically throughout the ship's hull and its decks to ensure that it would sink in a gradual, level and uniform manner, according to a fact sheet ‌posted online by project organizers. No explosives were used. Passageways were ⁠also cut through the 12 decks of the interior to allow for marine life to thrive in and around the ship on the sea floor. If all goes as planned, the aging 20th-century vessel will come to rest upright on the gulf floor at a depth of 180 ⁠feet off the coast of Destin, Florida, a resort town and recreational fishing haven known for its white sand beaches and emerald green waters. The upper deck is expected to end up about 50 feet beneath the surface, organizers said. SINKING STARTS SLOWLY The sinking process began at about 1 p.m. CST but was so imperceptibly slow that the majority of the ocean liner's hull remained well above the surface ​as ​the sun set on the idle ship, surrounded by blinking lights of nearby vessels. After hours, during which ​the waterline was seen creeping up the ship's hull inches at a ‌time, the sinking accelerated as the sea poured through the holes cut into the lower decks and flooded the interior. In the final moments, livestream footage showed the ship abruptly listing to its port side before gently rolling into the sea and disappearing. Warren Jones, a spokesperson for organizers, who watched the sinking from an observation boat, said the SS United States would probably take 30 to 60 minutes to reach the seabed once the interior compartments were all completely filled with water. The SS United States, a wonder of post-World War Two oceanic luxury and engineering that carried the rich and famous across the Atlantic at speeds still unmatched, was retired from service in 1969 amid the rising popularity of commercial air travel. The ‌vessel sat moored for nearly 30 years in Philadelphia, seemingly destined to be sold for scrap, before ​authorities in Okaloosa County, in Florida's panhandle, stepped in to purchase the ship as part of a $13 million ​project. "We worked year after year to keep that ship from going to the ​scrap yard," said Jones, a boyhood passenger of the ship and representative of the SS United States Conservancy, a group that sold the ship ‌to Okaloosa County. After obtaining permission from the US Coast Guard and other ​agencies, the county had the vessel towed to ​a shipyard in Mobile, Alabama, where it was prepared for disposal at sea. The SS United States will be in good company, joining a collection of more than 500 smaller underwater sites created from the remains of various sunken ships and concrete structures to create a divers' haven known as the Destin-Fort Walton Beach Artificial Reefs. Speaking ​with Reuters by phone on Wednesday night, Jones said some wreck ‌divers were already gearing up to explore the sunken remnants of the ocean liner as early as Thursday morning. Jones, recounting vivid memories of riding the ship ​as an 8-year-old passenger with his family in 1961, said he was "comforted seeing it settle on the floor of the gulf and being embraced by ​the sea." (Reporting by Steve Gorman in Los Angeles; Editing by Stephen Coates and Tom Hogue) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/famed-ship-heads-afterlife-artificial-003800609.html

articles.title: Alaska judge rules Mary Peltola's request for ballot data in Senate race is 'not reasonable'
articles.summary: JUNEAU, Alaska (AP) — An Alaska judge ruled Wednesday that a request by Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Mary Peltola's campaign for a list of absentee voters whose ballots have been rejected is “not reasonable,” particularly given the time crunch election officials face as they continue counting ballots from last week's election. Ballots are still being tallied in the ranked vote election, in which Peltola and two-term Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan are the main contenders. Alaska’s is the only Senate race in the country that remained too early to call. The state accepts ballots up to 15 days after general elections from overseas voters, making Nov. 18 the final day to receive them. That date is also the Division of Elections’ target for conducting ranked vote tabulations if no candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes. Attorneys for Peltola’s campaign last Friday sued state elections officials, seeking a list of voters whose absentee ballots have been rejected and the reasons for the rejections. They said their intent was to ensure that all qualified voters have their ballots counted. But attorneys for the state said the information requested would violate voter privacy. They also said producing such a list from a voter database would constitute an “electronic service or product” that under state law may not take priority over an agency's main responsibilities. Superior Court Judge Thomas Matthews, in a written ruling, said that “in theory” records from the voter database could be redacted and produced in a way that would allow their release. But he said the division is not required to disclose the records requested by the campaign because they “cannot reasonably be produced at this juncture, nor redacted of confidential information.” The division has deadlines to meet and says its staff is working long hours to accomplish the agency's “fundamental responsibility” of administering elections, he wrote. “The timing of the Campaign's request could simply not be worse,” Matthews wrote. An email seeking comment from one of the law firms representing Peltola's campaign was not immediately returned Wednesday, which was a holiday. The state Department of Law, which represented the Division of Elections, in a statement said it was pleased with Matthews' decision. Abha Khanna, an attorney for Peltola’s campaign, said during arguments Tuesday before Matthews the campaign wasn’t seeking to disrupt the ballot counting process. She said the absentee ballot review process was going “incredibly smoothly.” But Khanna argued the information sought is a matter of public record and in line with what campaign observers have access to in locations where absentee review boards are meeting. The campaign wanted access to that information in a more centralized way, she said. Attorneys for the state have argued that reports generated by the division with lists of ballots to be reviewed during the absentee ballot review process are not public records because they contain confidential information and are “ephemeral working documents that are not meant for preservation.” Michaela Thompson, who oversees the absentee ballot review boards for the division, said in an affidavit that the version of the report received by observers of the review process — including those affiliated with the campaigns — does not include as much confidential information but does include home addresses that many voters seek to keep private. The observers sign confidentiality agreements and cannot keep, copy or record information in the report, she said. The division’s “old, inflexible” database cannot produce a report that excludes confidential addresses, meaning the agency would have to work with a vendor to create a more tailored report, Thompson said. articles.title: Nvidia reportedly preparing to oust CEO after 2nd affair allegation emerges
articles.summary: Embattled Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang was allegedly involved in a second extramarital affair. The company's board is reportedly meeting to determine if it will oust Huang as chief executive, the Wall Street Journal reports . Nvidia stock fell in after-hours trading following the report. According to The New York Times , Huang, whose relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy has embroiled the company in scandal this week, also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell. She joined Nvidia in 2008 and heads up the company's healthcare business. The Times report says that Huang and Powell were seen being affectionate at a hotel during a company conference in March, and that when a bystander took a photo of the interaction, a security guard "sequestered them" and made them an offer to sign a nondisclosure agreement. Last month, The Times reported that US intelligence services believed a woman, Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, may have acted as an intelligence asset , sharing information with the ruling party in Beijing. On Sunday, Huang issued a statement apologizing to his family and Nvidia employees for having an affair, though he didn't name with whom. In response, Nvidia's board said it is launching an independent investigation into the matter. "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," the board said in a statement Sunday. articles.title: Democrats frustrated by absences in failed Hegseth impeachment vote
articles.summary: From left: Nancy Pelosi, Steven Horsford and Haley Stevens missed the vote on Tuesday evening. Composite: Getty Images, Bloomberg Democratic lawmakers expressed outrage at nearly a dozen of their colleagues for missing a vote Tuesday evening to impeach the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth , allowing Republicans to defeat the effort. Eleven Democrats missed the key procedural vote on the impeachment effort , which failed by just seven votes. Some blamed traffic and conflicting events and others accused Speaker Mike Johnson of closing the vote early. Many of those not in the Capitol said they support the effort to impeach Hegseth. “You should show up and do your job,” Abdul El-Sayed , the senator-elect of Michigan, said on CNN to the Democratic lawmakers Tuesday. Richard Ojeda, the representative-elect of North Carolina, told CNN that the Democratic representatives “failed” by not voting. “Shame on them for not showing up,” Ojeda said on Tuesday. “I mean, this is important … they had an opportunity to finally get rid of this buffoonery we had.” The missing Democrats gave House Republicans the numbers to shelve the impeachment effort by voting 211 – 204 to refer eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth to a House committee. Speaking at Arlington national cemetery to mark Veterans Day, Donald Trump praised Hegseth and said he had done a “fantastic job” as the Pentagon head. “I had a feeling that was going to happen,” the president said of the failed effort to impeach Hegseth, adding: “He loves you, and he protects you – he’s all about you.” The articles, introduced by Republican Thomas Massie , included charges of violating congressional authority by waging war in Iran . The effort came after voters overwhelming cast ballots for Democratic candidates in the 2026 midterms, largely in rebuke of the Trump administration’s policies – including the war in Iran. Sydney Kamlager-Dove, a representative from California, told MeidasTouch there was “no reason why we should have lost this vote because of attendance issues”. “This is what the people have been talking about … so shame on folks who were not here because these people lost,” Kamlager-Dove added. Melanie Stansbury of New Mexico wrote on X that she was “blocked from entering the Capitol to vote due to a traffic incident and a police escort of a bus during the vote”. “When she reached the chamber the vote had just gaveled out. She immediately filed a report of her vote of ‘NO’ to the motion meant to kill the impeachment articles and refer them to the Judiciary Committee, as documented in the Congressional Record,” Stansbury wrote, adding that Hegseth “must be impeached now”. Laura Gillen of New York similarly wrote on X she too was stuck in traffic but “strongly” believes Hegseth should be impeached. Jonathan Jackson, of Illinois, wrote on X that he also was stuck behind the traffic jam. Brittany Pettersen of Colorado wrote on X that she was “denied” the ability to vote. A member of Pettersen’s office later told 9News she too was stuck in traffic. Julia Brownley of California wrote on Facebook that Johnson “closed the vote” before she could make it to the House floor. “As I and many of my colleagues were rushing to the floor to support Hegseth’s impeachment, Mike Johnson closed the vote before we could,” Brownley wrote. Marilyn Strickland of Washington also missed the vote by one minute because she was stuck behind a motocade, but that she would have voted to impeach Hegseth, Strickland’s office told Politico . Nancy Pelosi of California missed the vote because she was in San Francisco to meet with local veterans and accept a Lifetime Advocate for Veterans Award, Pelosi’s spokesperson told SFGate . Lou Correa of California wrote on Instagram that he was undergoing a medical procedure and remaining in his district until he was medically cleared. Steven Horsford of Nevada, Haley Stevens of Michigan and Frederica Wilson of Florida did not provide public reasons for their absence on Tuesday. Several Democratic lawmakers who did vote on the effort to impeach Hegseth noted that they were also busy with other life events but still made their way to the Capitol. Pat Ryan of New York wrote on X that he was recovering from back surgery but left the hospital early in order to cast his vote. Congressman Glenn Ivey, a Maryland Democrat, called the absence of the 11 lawmakers during Tuesday’s vote “certainly disappointing”, but said there would be “other chances” to advance impeachment efforts. In an interview, Ivey said he was “absolutely” supportive of renewing the push when Democrats regain control of both chambers in January. At the same time, he argued that voters made clear that concerns about the cost of living remain their top priority. “There aren’t a lot of people, in my district anyway, [whose ability] to stay in their house depends on whether Hegseth gets impeached or not,” Ivey said. “We’ve been calling it the affordability agenda, but I think for many people, it’s really a survivability agenda, and we need to be focused on that.” • This story was updated on 11 November 2026. A previous version incorrectly stated that Brittany Pettersen is a lawmaker from California; she is from Colorado. articles.title: Ole Miss students speak out after viral video of alleged racist taunts
articles.summary: The Black college students who were harassed by two White students at the University of Mississippi making monkey gestures and sounds outside their apartment are speaking out after the incident went viral. The women said they were familiar with the stories of racism some faced at Ole Miss over the years — the school didn't allow its first Black student, James Meredith, until 1962, for instance — but they were not prepared for what they experienced last Friday. Jakirya Metcalf, a freshman at Ole Miss, said she was in her apartment last Friday night when she saw the video on her Ring camera . "We actually went outside and tried to, like, approach them and get them to explain why they did that," Metcalf told "CBS Mornings." "One girl was like, 'I'm sorry we did that to four doors,'" Victoria Johnson, one of the roommates, said. "And mind you, we didn't see any one of those doors. It was just ours that was targeted. And she was like, 'We didn't mean any harm.'" Metcalf and Johnson said the first person seen on the video, Aliana Kunes, apologized. But the second person, who made monkey sounds toward the camera, doubled down off-camera. "She continued to make the gestures after the girl was apologizing," Johnson said. "It was like a slap in the face." "I had said that I don't think they should go around because even if they go to other people's door and do that, I don't think they should do that because it's very disrespectful," Metcalf said. Kunes apologized for her actions in a statement Tuesday. "To the women I offended and to the Ole Miss community, I sincerely apologize," she wrote. "Before the incident on November 6, I never met the women involved and was unaware of their race, however, I recognize my actions were insensitive, inappropriate, and deeply harmful. I would have never intentionally made those noises or gestures toward a person of color. I have apologized to the women and I pray they will forgive me." Kunes voluntarily withdrew from the university after issuing the statement Tuesday. When asked if she accepted Kunes' apology, Metcalf said she had mixed feelings. "I feel like no matter like who we are, or if she knew our race or not, but the gestures and the voices, I feel like it still was very disrespectful," she said. "I appreciate the apology, but I feel like it still doesn't change what happened on that Friday, because it's still hurtful and it's still devastating that someone would come to our camera and do that," Kaiyden Caldwell, another of the roommates, told "CBS Mornings." Johnson's mother, Chiquita Laó, said she was surprised to learn Kunes withdrew from the university after Kunes said she was harassed. "I hate to hear that because you know the children are the future, but I feel like everybody needs to be accountable," Laó said. University officials said in a statement they are investigating the incident and have spoken with those targeted. "The university has been and will continue providing care and resources to our students," the school said in a statement on Wednesday. "We have met with the impacted students and their families to offer support and discuss the relevant processes, and the investigation is moving forward. Student privacy laws prohibit the university from commenting on any specific student, including any potential disciplinary action." Metcalf, Caldwell and Johnson said they plan to stay at Ole Miss and said they won't let the incident ruin their time at the school. CBS News reached out to the two other women in the video but did not hear back. "I want people to be mindful of their actions now," Johnson said. "So when people who would potentially experience the same situations to speak out and don't let things be swept under the rug, because this is a reality for us, and I feel like voices need to be heard." articles.title: Hegseth's group reprimanded by guard at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
articles.summary: A US Army sentinel guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier admonished Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his entourage Wednesday after some in the group laughed and talked near the solemn memorial following a Veterans Day ceremony. “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times!” the sentinel called out, stopping his patrol to face the group as they departed - CNN A US Army sentinel guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier reprimanded Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and a group of his senior advisers Wednesday after some in the group laughed and talked near the solemn memorial following a Veterans Day ceremony. “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times,” the sentinel called out, stopping his patrol to face the group as they departed. Hegseth was standing and taking photos in front of the tomb with his wife, Jennifer, chief of staff Ricky Buria, deputy chief of staff Patrick Weaver and senior adviser and deputy assistant Tami Radabaugh after the ceremony held at Arlington National Cemetery for Veterans Day. Some in the group were laughing and chatting after taking photos, prompting the soldier patrolling in front of the Tomb to yell out and correct them. When asked for comment, Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the “soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum.” “The Secretary and the entire Department have always honored—and will always honor—the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe. While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum,” Parnell said. The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is one of the most sacred war memorials in the US, marking the final resting place of an unknown soldier who was killed in World War I. A soldier assigned to The Old Guard, or 3rd Infantry Regiment, has been guarding the tomb around the clock, rain or shine, since 1948. Foreign dignitaries, presidents, public figures and politicians frequently visit the Tomb to pay their respects to American service members. Hegseth and his team were at Arlington National Cemetery for a ceremony that was also attended by President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance. The defense secretary had been under renewed scrutiny and pressure in recent days after articles of impeachment were filed against him by outgoing GOP Rep. Thomas Massie. But in a procedural vote on Tuesday night, the GOP successfully blocked the impeachment process from moving forward, prompting Hegseth and his allies to claim vindication. Hegseth stood accused by Massie of executing unlawful orders, including by waging war in Iran without congressional approval, ignoring laws about minimizing civilian casualties, and directing the Pentagon to carry out extrajudicial killings. In a press conference on Tuesday, Hegseth said the charges amounted to a policy dispute and not high crimes and misdemeanors. President Donald Trump, who also faced criticism for behavior at Arlington National Cemetery when he filmed a campaign video there in 2024, stood by Hegseth leading up to Tuesday’s vote and vowed to continue supporting him moving forward. The developing system unfolded across the Great Lakes and Ohio Valley on Wednesday, bringing a threat of severe weather to parts of the region. The rain will then spread farther inland across Pennsylvania and into upstate New York. It is expected that travel impacts could escalate late Thursday into Friday as the winds pick up, and the rain becomes heavier. When Is The Earliest Snowfall On Record For Parts Of The Northeast? Outside higher elevations, snowfall totals will generally remain below 3 inches, with amounts decreasing farther south. Some snow is expected across valley cities. Persistent northwest winds off the lake will help generate several inches of snow, with totals potentially exceeding half a foot in some locations. articles.title: A 67-year-old Democratic veteran is becoming the left's favorite to replace Schumer
articles.summary: Progressive lawmakers and activists are hoping to harness momentum from last week’s sweeping Democratic victories to install inspiring new congressional leaders. Many have looked at the Senate and found their guy: a 67-year-old father of three from an affluent Washington suburb who has held public office continuously since 1991. Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland has emerged as the alternative of choice for a swath of Democrats who believe Chuck Schumer, the longtime Senate Democratic leader, should step aside despite presiding over massive midterm gains. It’s the culmination of a remarkable resurgence for Van Hollen, who spent years inching up the Democratic leadership ladder in the House only to ditch his seniority there for the back benches of the Senate in 2017. Over the past two years, he has emerged as an increasingly strident critic of the Democratic party establishment and its approach to President Donald Trump, as well as its positions on populist economic policies and the U.S. relationship with Israel — and members of the party’s left flank have noticed. A wave of House Democrats, outside activists and even at least one newly elected senator are effectively trying to draft him into what could be an uphill race to unseat the 75-year-old Schumer as majority leader. “I have been very impressed by Senator Van Hollen’s leadership,” said Sen.-elect Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota, who beat a more centrist Democrat in her state’s primary and has said she will not back Schumer. Van Hollen has wavered on whether he is pursuing a role in Senate leadership or perhaps instead a 2028 run for the presidency. He said Tuesday he is “actively listening” as he keeps the door open to a majority leader bid ahead of the early December caucus elections. “I’m trying to talk to our members, and I think it’s important to reach out to everybody,” he said in the Capitol halls. Flanagan said she had not had “formal conversations” with Van Hollen, but another younger Democrat — Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan — met with him this week as she called for a leadership shakeup. Outside the building, at a gathering of progressive groups charting an agenda for the coming Democratic majorities, Van Hollen was sharply critical of the existing Senate Democratic power structure — and Schumer in particular. “We just saw democracy in America in action — we should bring a little more democracy to the United States Senate,” he said, before later accusing Schumer and the Senate Democratic campaign arm of having “sided with the crypto industry and AIPAC” to oppose more progressive candidates in this year’s primaries. That outspokenness has gotten Van Hollen noticed on the left — and it has been especially striking coming from a son of prominent U.S. diplomats who spent decades dutifully rising through the Democratic Party establishment and chaired both the House and Senate campaign committees. “Van Hollen represents a bridge between the old guard — people who’ve been in office for a long time with a more moderate orientation — and the new generation that is coming into office,” said Joseph Geevarghese, executive director of Our Revolution. His rhetoric and actions have evolved dramatically, however, since Trump returned to office in 2025. The administration’s spending cuts decimated Van Hollen’s constituency — particularly in his political base of Montgomery County — and his posts on the Appropriations and Foreign Relations committees gave him a front-row seat to Trump’s elimination of USAID. Meanwhile, he became an outspoken critic of the White House’s mass deportation agenda and was the first U.S. lawmaker to visit the El Salvador prison where the administration was sending scores of deportees — including a Maryland man, Kilmar Ábrego García, who had been mistakenly deported in contravention of a court order. Van Hollen has also become increasingly critical of the U.S. posture toward Israel, joining early Democratic pushes to restrict arms sales to Benjamin Netanyahu’s government as its war on Gaza after the 2023 Hamas attacks grew increasingly brutal. “He’s been correct,” said Jeff Cohen, founder of RootsAction, a group pushing its members to back Van Hollen over Schumer. “He’s been with the base of the party on most issues: redefining the U.S.-Israel relationship is one. Taxing the wealthy is another, standing up to AI — all of these issues that Schumer is wrong on.” Van Hollen’s approach to the Senate leadership race has evolved in recent days. He downplayed a bid for top leader earlier this year, including saying in a recent interview that it has “not been my focus.” The day after the election, Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed appeared to believe he had passed on a run, calling Van Hollen “my white whale” in response to a question about his ideal Senate leader. But asked about the matter Tuesday as the drumbeat for his candidacy grew, Van Hollen said there should not be a “coronation” for Schumer as he described his ongoing listening tour. “We should not support anybody for leader without a very clear plan and as you know, there are many people who think that a change is required,” he said. A Senate aide who was granted anonymity to describe Van Hollen’s thinking said the senator has been influenced by the scale of his party’s midterm victory and the calls he has heard for change — as well as the public outreach he is getting. The aide said Van Hollen is not coordinating the outside effort to nudge him into challenging Schumer. Senate Democrats still broadly expect Schumer to be reelected as leader, and some are openly warning Van Hollen away from jumping into the race. “I'm going to vote for Schumer. He helped recruit a great class, and I can't imagine why you would vote for someone like Van Hollen with no record of doing anything,” pro-Israel Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.) told reporters. Asked about whether Van Hollen will run, Fetterman added, “I dare him to.” Schumer’s backers point to his decades of fundraising experience, deep well of relationships within the caucus and across the party, and his work to unite his colleagues and battle Trump over the past year. And with Democrats poised to pick up as many as nine seats — a once-unthinkable outcome — they are questioning why senators would depose the leader who helped make it happen. "When the manager takes you to the World Series, you give him another contract,” Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.) said Tuesday at a joint news conference with Schumer. But those arguments are carrying little water with those who view Schumer as out of touch with the direction of the party. They note that while he supported the incoming freshmen with hundreds of millions of dollars of general-election spending, he opposed some of them during the primary. Van Hollen could be using his flirtations with a bid to influence some end-of-year decisionmaking. He is pushing Congress to cut off Iran war funding as they head toward a Dec. 11 government funding deadline, and he wants a provision mandating cooperation with Israel stripped from the annual defense policy bill. Those stances could help push Schumer and the party into a more confrontational posture, which Van Hollen signaled he wanted in an interview earlier this year. “It’s going to be very important that Democrats let voters know not only what we’re against but what we stand for,” he said. “And I think a lot of voters, you know, think Democrats have been too much finger-in-the-wind. They’ve been too wishy-washy.” Grace Yarrow and Lisa Kashinsky contributed to this report. articles.summary: 马斯克与多位商界领袖公开呼吁英伟达董事会不要在调查结束前解雇黄仁勋，并要求把去留决定交给股东。一桩个人私德风波，正在演变为牵动公司治理、股东权利与AI交易走向的市场事件。 当地时间11月11日晚间，《纽约时报》曝出黄仁勋的第二段婚外情——与下属金伯利·鲍威尔的恋爱关系。随后《华尔街日报》报道，英伟达董事会已成立由独立董事主导、外部律师参与的调查委员会，并正在准备解除黄仁勋的职务。部分董事倾向由首席财务官Colette Kress出任过渡期CEO，同时公司已委托外部猎头机构启动新CEO搜寻工作。 面对潜在的领导层更迭，多位科技巨头与风投机构高管通过社交媒体平台呼吁英伟达董事会保持克制。Atreides Management管理合伙人兼首席投资官Gavin Baker提出 “调查结束后由股东投票”方案，马斯克对此以“正是如此”回应 ；Epic Games创始人兼首席执行官Tim Sweeney喊出 “拯救黄仁勋” ；太阳微系统联合创始人、风险投资人Vinod Khosla附议投资人Ron Conway的 “耐心等待调查结束”。 突然的领导层动荡引发了投资者的强烈担忧，直接冲击了资本市场。英伟达盘后股价大幅下跌8%。 “拯救黄仁勋”！大佬集体发声 针对董事会可能采取的单方面行动，商界大佬对其是否符合股东利益提出质疑。Gavin Baker表示，英伟达董事会应等待调查结果，并在调查完成后举行股东投票。他指出， 在盘后股价大跌8%的情况下，很难论证解雇黄仁勋符合股东的最佳利益。 这一立场迅速获得了科技界重量级人物的支持。马斯克在社交媒体X上回复以示赞同。 LAUNCH创办人Jason Calacanis也强调， 更好的解决方案是完成调查，且应由英伟达股东在调查完成后决定黄仁勋的去留，而不是由媒体或网民决定。 他透露自己持有英伟达多头仓位并刚刚加仓，同时呼吁董事会在当前价位大规模回购股票。 Epic Games创始人兼首席执行官则Tim Sweeney在X上写道： “拯救黄仁勋。如果英伟达董事会真这么做，将是堪比苹果解雇史蒂夫·乔布斯的愚蠢 ，也是对美国的严重伤害。从游戏显卡时代到CUDA再到人工智能超级计算机，这家伙确实是驱动科技未来的远见者。” 他在另一条帖子中把矛头指向替代方案，称用公司的“管钱的人”替换这个时代领先的技术远见者荒谬至极，董事会这样做等于以股东的代价把公司烧掉。 Vinod Khosla的表态只有一句“赞同Ron！”，所赞同的是投资人Ron Conway在《华尔街日报》报道之前说过的话： “在风波仍在持续（我认为应当认真对待）的时候，让我们先停一下，记住黄仁勋以他的决心和远见为我们这个行业作出的贡献，那是我们今天共同工作的基础。” Ron Conway还称，黄仁勋的表态对他的家人和整个行业都展现了风度和尊严： “现在我们应该耐心等待董事会和有关政府部门的调查结束”。 前Coinbase首席技术官Balaji Srinivasan的类比更直白： “不。比尔·克林顿没有辞职。黄仁勋也不该辞职。英伟达董事会不该解雇他。尤其是在事态正热的时候。扛过去，别管那些记者。” 对冲基金经理Bill Ackman此前在X上写道：“黄仁勋是人，而且是了不起的人。了不起的人也会犯错。他已承担责任，大家应支持他和他的家人。”他随后补充：“我喜欢这人，他为世界做了很多好事。我希望这只是一场简单的出轨” 半导体研究机构SemiAnalysis创始人兼CEO Dylan Patel在X上表示：“接下来6个月，黄仁勋不会发生任何事，这个故事在媒体/金融界将基本平息。但民主党人会把他召到国会，他们会彻底调查对相关公司的GPU销售情况，然后用一堆问题猛击他。那才是靴子/可能/落下的时刻。” 6票悬念：董事会能不能代表股东 真正决定黄仁勋去留的，是董事会的票数，而不是X上的声量。 英伟达董事会现有11人，除创始人黄仁勋外，其他10人是独立董事。按2024年3月修订的公司内部规章第32条，任何高管可随时由当时在任董事的过半数罢免，有因无因都可以。11人在任，过半数就是6票。普通议案只需出席董事过半数，罢免高管则按在任董事总数计算，门槛更严一些。 黄仁勋本人投反对票也没用，其余10名独立董事里有6票就够了。 公司股票一股一票，没有超级投票权。问题在于，黄仁勋受益持股3.58%，其他十名董事总持股约0.31%。换句话说，真走到董事会投票决定罢免黄仁勋那一步，他的去留将由并不充分代表股东权益的董事会成员决定。 资本端的担忧则更贴近持仓。据市场讨论，华尔街担心黄仁勋会辞职，“很多基金经理将在未来几周减持英伟达”。与之相对，散户视角更多指向先例—— articles.title: AI服务器+iPhone Duo双驱动，鸿海Q3净利润大增34%超预期
articles.summary: 鸿海精密工业第三季度净利润大幅超越市场预期，创下历史新高，AI服务器业务的强劲增长与苹果折叠屏手机iPhone Duo的旺盛需求共同构成双轮驱动。 鸿海周四（11月12日）公布的数据显示， 截至9月的三个月内，净利润同比增长34%至775亿新台币（约24亿美元），高于分析师平均预期的703亿新台币。 此前，公司已披露同期营收季增47%，达到创纪录的3.03万亿新台币。AI服务器组装已成为鸿海增长的最大引擎，推动公司加速突破对消费电子业务的传统依赖。 鸿海董事长刘扬伟称， 存储芯片及零部件短缺问题仍将持续到2027年 ，预计2027年营收将实现两位数增长。刘杨伟表示，将于2027年向Neocloud（新云）公司销售更多服务器。 上调旗下四大产品类别的业绩预期， 公司对2027年的业务前景持谨慎乐观态度。 然而，围绕英伟达首席执行黄仁勋婚外情丑闻的持续发酵，令市场对全球AI基础设施建设前景产生疑虑，作为英伟达核心服务器组装合作伙伴，鸿海面临潜在的不确定性。与此同时，投资者对AI资本支出增速放缓的担忧持续压制鸿海股价，公司股价自6月高点已累计下跌逾20%，市值缩水至略超1000亿美元。 AI服务器需求强劲，营收季增创纪录 AI服务器业务的爆发式增长是本季度鸿海业绩的核心驱动力。 财报显示，鸿海第三季度营收大概率同比飙升47%至创纪录的3.03万亿新台币，环比增长约20%，云计算与网络业务引领增长，主要受益于英伟达GB系列AI服务器机架的持续出货、超大规模云厂商资本支出的提升以及产能的持续扩张。 鸿海是英伟达的主要服务器组装合作伙伴，受益于搭载英伟达GPU（包括下一代Rubin芯片）的AI服务器需求激增。彭博分析师Steven Tseng和Sean Chen指出，强劲的运营杠杆效应、更高的自动化水平以及垂直整合的深化，将支撑利润增长，并有助于抵消毛利率摊薄压力。 据彭博报道，鸿海董事长刘扬伟10月表示，公司目标在两年内夺取AI服务器市场50%的份额，并通过生产更多高附加值零部件，将毛利率提升至约10%。 iPhone Duo贡献增量，高端消费电子回暖 在AI服务器之外，苹果折叠屏手机iPhone Duo的强劲需求为鸿海提供了重要的业绩支撑。苹果将该设备的初期市场反响定性为“非凡”，鸿海（即富士康）负责在中国及印度工厂组装iPhone Duo及iPhone 18系列。 彭博智库预计，iPhone Duo从现在至明年9月的累计销量最高可达1600万部。苹果与鸿海均寄望于iPhone Duo等高端产品提振利润率——这一策略的背景是，全球智能手机整体出货量目前徘徊于2013年以来的最低水平。 彭博分析师指出，智能消费电子业务受益于iPhone新品发布及更高的销售均价，季节性复苏态势明显。 在主营业务之外，鸿海过去三个月进一步加码电动车产业布局。公司宣布以7.27亿美元收购三菱电机旗下汽车零部件业务50%的股权，持续推进从消费电子代工向高附加值制造领域的战略转型。 彭博分析师指出，高附加值AI服务器占比的持续提升将对毛利率形成摊薄效应，但选择性采用寄售安排有望缓解相关压力，强劲的运营杠杆与垂直整合深化将为利润增长提供支撑。 尽管业绩亮眼，投资者对AI建设热潮持续性的疑虑仍是悬在鸿海头顶的一把利剑。数据中心行业债务驱动扩张的模式已显现压力迹象，大型AI开发商尚未证明其商业模式具备可持续盈利能力，超大规模云厂商的资本支出增速在多年快速扩张后面临放缓预期。 与此同时，英伟达CEO黄仁勋婚外情的报道持续发酵，外界对这位AI基础设施建设重要推手的前景产生质疑，作为英伟达关键供应商的鸿海亦难以置身事外。受上述因素叠加影响，鸿海股价自6月峰值已累计下跌逾20%，市值降至略超1000亿美元。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 机构预计Anthropic上市首日散户净买入约2.5亿美元，或达SpaceX纪录两倍
articles.summary: Vanda Research预计，Anthropic上市首日有望录得约 2.5亿美元散户净买入 ，若成真，将是SpaceX所创1.18亿美元纪录的两倍，并可能跻身历史上规模最大的单日散户买入之列。 据媒体11月12日报道，Vanda Research周三（11月11日）公布的报告显示，这一测算基于该机构对历次新股上市首日散户交易行为的分析，以及Hyperliquid平台上Anthropic IPO前永续期货的成交规模。该机构全球宏观策略师Viraj Patel在报告中称： “从IPO前永续期货的交易看，Anthropic正朝着一场纪录级的散户IPO演进。” 这一判断的市场影响主要在于量级。Vanda数据显示， 2024年以来仅有六只股票的单日散户买入额突破2.5亿美元 ，该机构称Anthropic“下周可能吸引到我们数据中罕见规模的散户买盘”。 Anthropic此次IPO目标估值最高1.4万亿美元，股票预计 11月19日在纳斯达克开始交易 ；公司已将募资目标下调至644亿美元，发行价区间拟定70至78美元，并通过RetailBook向英国散户开放认购。 测算基于上市日交易行为和永续合约成交 Vanda的2.5亿美元并非取自认购簿或承销数据，而是把两件事放在一起观察：一是历史上新股上市首日散户资金的流入规律，二是Hyperliquid上相关合约的交易热度。前者提供基准，后者提供这次IPO的“预热强度”。SpaceX的1.18亿美元纪录是这套框架下的对照物，对Anthropic的测算结果则是它的两倍。 需要区分的是，IPO前永续期货是在Hyperliquid、Coinbase等交易所交易的一类衍生品合约，交易者借此对非上市公司的估值下注。 这类合约与标的股份没有直接挂钩，其定价只参考公司最新披露的上市前估值。 因此，合约层面的成交活跃度反映的是市场对估值的预期与分歧，并非对上市股份的直接认购，也不能直接换算成配售需求。 按Vanda的统计，2024年以来单日散户买入超过2.5亿美元的股票只有六只。把门槛设在这一水平，说明该机构的判断是“散户会以极少数个案才有的规模涌入”，而不只是“散户会来”。这一判断最终能否兑现，仍取决于上市首日的实际资金流向；测算本身仍属预估。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 油轮运费腰斩，战争溢价退潮：油市进入协议验证期？
articles.summary: 11月初美国中期选举民主党大胜后，市场对美伊重启谈判、推动地区局势缓和的预期显著升温。特朗普随后释放克制信号，称“极不可能”立即对伊朗发动大规模军事打击，但同时强调最终取决于伊朗是否接受一项足够强硬的协议。受上述政治信号影响，市场开始重估此前已计入油价的战争风险溢价。 布油期货迅速自10月30日117美元/桶的高位回落，一度大跌超20%至93美元/桶附近（目前布油价格91.9美元/桶），创下自2020年4月以来的最大单周跌幅之一。油轮运费也随之暴跌。美国墨西哥湾至亚洲租用超级油轮（VLCC）成本从一个月前7960万美元降至4500万美元，跌幅约43.5%；折合单桶原油运费从近39.8美元大幅降至22.5美元。 与此同时，美湾至欧洲阿芙拉型（Aframax）原油油轮运费已连续十个交易日下跌，创两个月新低。此前该航线运费较战前飙升近8倍，一度占原油到岸成本25%以上；运费与油价同步急挫，地缘恐慌驱动的极端航运溢价正被快速挤出。 运费下降有望重新打开远距离原油贸易窗口，推动实物市场进一步修复 9月底中东原油出口已恢复至战前约9成，但油价仍处高位。原因便在于运费、保险及航运风险溢价高企；同时，霍尔木兹海峡约92%的过境船只以关闭AIS的暗船方式航行，反映彼时航运正常化程度有限，风险溢价由此得以维持。

articles.title: 豆包工作全面开放多模型 ，办公Agent“路由大战”再升级
articles.summary: 字节跳动旗下的豆包工作，开始让用户使用更多竞争对手的大模型。 11月12日，豆包工作宣布更新模型阵容，在原有豆包2.1 Lite和Pro两款自研模型之外，正式接入Kimi K3.1 Pro、GLM 5.3、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash等第三方模型。 这次更新还伴随着一轮价格调整。 豆包工作将在模型选择页面标注不同模型的额度消耗倍率，用户可以根据任务复杂程度、响应速度及使用成本，自主选择模型。同时，平台还推出限时优惠计划，下调豆包2.1 Lite和DeepSeek V4.1 Flash的额度消耗倍率，并向新用户提供30天免费订阅权益。 事实上，豆包工作在10月29日就已率先向团队及企业订阅客户开放第三方模型服务。此次进一步更新模型阵容和优惠机制，也让多模型策略成为豆包工作争夺用户的重要手段。 豆包工作的转变或许来自市场竞争的压力。 此前，腾讯WorkBuddy已经接入混元、GLM、MiniMax、Kimi、DeepSeek等多家模型厂商的产品，并通过Auto模式，根据路由策略自动选择适合的模型。 WorkBuddy确实建立一定的领先优势。易观分析发布的2026年三季度办公智能体市场报告显示，今年9月，WorkBuddy的月访问量达到8534万次，豆包工作则为3039万次，前者约为后者的2.8倍。 在WorkBuddy持续扩大用户规模、抢占办公Agent入口的背景下，豆包工作也面临着越来越直接的竞争压力。 事实上，字节并非没有多模型产品的经验。早在豆包工作开放第三方模型之前，字节旗下从AI编程工具起步的TRAE就已经采取多模型策略，其TRAE Work同样提供Seed、GLM、DeepSeek、Kimi、MiniMax等不同厂商的模型选择，并支持用户自行接入模型服务。 行业情况来看，百度也采取了类似的开放策略。今年8月，百度将文库、网盘联合推出的通用智能体GenFlow正式更名为库库AI，并推出独立办公客户端及企业版。 其中，库库AI的模型选择列表中，除了百度自研的文心大模型，还包括DeepSeek、GLM、Kimi、MiniMax等第三方模型。 阿里旗下的Qoder也是如此。今年4月，Qoder社区版正式开放自带API Key接入能力，支持阿里云百炼、智谱、DeepSeek、Kimi、MiniMax等多家模型服务商，但千问办公迄今未开放第三方模型。 多模型与单一模型策略背后是Agent产品与传统AI聊天工具之间的差异。 对于普通聊天产品而言，模型的知识储备、推理能力及生成质量，往往直接影响用户体验。但Agent需要处理的任务更加复杂，一个任务可能涉及资料搜集、文档分析、代码编写、数据处理，以及最终结果的生成和验证。 不同模型在这些环节的表现并不相同，使用成本也存在差异。 对办公Agent平台而言，能否接入最强模型固然重要，但如何为不同任务匹配合适的模型，正在成为新的竞争变量。 比多模型接入更值得关注的是模型路由技术的发展。 目前，豆包工作的此次更新主要解决的是用户自主选择模型的问题。用户可以根据不同模型的特点和额度消耗倍率，决定把任务交给谁执行。 但用户手动选择模型并不是多模型架构的终点。 例如一名员工让Agent完成一份行业研究报告，整个过程可能包括搜集公开资料、整理财务数据、分析行业趋势以及制作演示文稿。 其中，基础信息整理可能只需要响应速度较快、成本较低的模型；涉及复杂财务分析或多步骤推理时，则需要调用能力更强的模型；到了格式调整等环节，又可以切换回成本更低的模型。 如果始终使用最昂贵的模型完成全部流程，可能造成不必要的算力消耗；但如果一味追求低成本，又可能因为模型能力不足而增加错误和返工。 模型路由要解决的正是如何在任务效果、执行速度与使用成本之间找到平衡。 这项能力已经开始进入办公Agent的产品架构。 腾讯WorkBuddy的Auto模式支持按照路由策略自动分配模型。在此之外，腾讯云还推出了独立的模型路由服务，可以根据请求意图、模型负载和响应延迟等因素，将任务分配给不同模型。 全天候科技注意到，此次豆包工作的Auto模式还采取小额免费的形式。 通过降低Auto模式的使用门槛，豆包工作有机会吸引更多用户尝试自动模型选择，让用户逐渐从自己挑选模型，转向直接交付任务、等待结果。 对平台而言，更多真实任务的执行也有助于持续评估不同模型的能力、成本和任务完成效果，为优化路由策略提供依据。 从这个角度看，豆包工作希望争取的可能不只是更多用户和任务量，还有未来办公Agent的模型调度权。 随着字节、腾讯、百度相继开放第三方模型，各家办公Agent能够调用的模型阵容正变得越来越相似。仅仅接入更多模型已经很难构成长期的差异化优势。 这也意味着，办公Agent的竞争正在进一步向模型之上的技术架构转移。 其中一项重要能力是模型路由，即根据任务难度、执行效果及Token成本，为不同任务分配合适的模型。而从更完整的Agent技术架构来看，模型路由只是其中一环。 近年来受到行业关注的Agent Harness，则进一步涉及任务规划、工具调用、上下文管理、执行状态维护及错误恢复等环节，决定Agent能否将模型能力转化为稳定的任务执行结果。 两者共同影响着办公Agent的商业化效率。 接下来各家是否会通过价格战的形式进一步吸引用户使用，正受到关注。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 报道：英伟达部分董事倾向由CFO Kress担任过渡期CEO
articles.summary: 英伟达董事会正准备罢免创始人兼CEO黄仁勋，部分董事倾向由首席财务官Colette Kress出任过渡期CEO，同时公司已委托外部猎头机构启动新CEO搜寻工作。 消息传出后，英伟达股价盘后跌逾8%，触及52周低点。 据美国媒体Semafor 12日援引知情人士透露，英伟达董事会定于美东时间本周三晚间召开会议，讨论是否最快于当天罢免黄仁勋。据Semafor报道，此次危机的导火索是媒体披露黄仁勋存在第二段婚外情。据一名美国政府高级官员透露，英伟达董事会已就此次计划召开的会议向白宫进行了通报。 此事引发的冲击已蔓延至政界。民主党参议员Chris Coons与Elizabeth Warren于周三联名致函特朗普内阁成员，要求各方保留与英伟达芯片出口相关的文件，并呼吁调查政府相关部门是否在已知晓安全隐患的情况下仍未采取行动。 过渡安排：Kress呼声较高，外部搜寻同步展开 据知情人士透露，若黄仁勋遭到罢免，英伟达董事会部分成员倾向于任命现任CFO Colette Kress担任过渡期CEO，但全体董事尚未就此作出最终决定。 与此同时，据彭博报道，英伟达已聘请外部猎头机构物色下一任CEO人选。据另一名知情人士透露，苹果硬件主管Johny Srouji是正在被考虑的候选人之一，他曾于2019年入围英特尔CEO候选人名单。 英伟达发言人未就上述事宜立即作出回应。 危机根源：婚外情疑云与安全调查 此次罢免议题是英伟达近期一系列风波的最新进展。黄仁勋此前公开承认存在婚外情，这家市值4万亿美元的公司随即陷入舆论与监管的双重压力之中。 英伟达长期任职的董事会已宣布委托律所Wachtell Lipton主导调查。作为全球人工智能基础设施的核心供应商，英伟达不仅向各大超大规模云计算企业提供最先进的芯片，还签署了数十亿美元的融资协议，深度参与AI基础设施的建设布局，使这一安全疑云的潜在影响更加复杂深远。 此案已引起国会关注。民主党参议员Chris Coons与Elizabeth Warren联名致函商务部长Howard Lutnick、国务卿Marco Rubio及白宫幕僚长Stephen Miller，要求其保存与英伟达芯片出口以及黄仁勋与特朗普往来通信相关的所有文件与记录。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
